tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on British & International Cuisine

questions.question: Q: Name three traditional British dishes.
questions.correctAnswer: Roast beef and Yorkshire pudding, fish and chips, shepherd's pie, full English breakfast, Sunday roast, trifle, Cornish pasty (any three).

questions.question: Q: How has multiculturalism changed the British diet?
questions.correctAnswer: Multiculturalism has introduced new ingredients, recipes, and cooking techniques from around the world, expanded supermarket ranges, created diverse restaurant options, and led to fusion cuisine. Chicken tikka masala is a prime example of this fusion.

questions.question: Q: What are the staple foods of Indian cuisine?
questions.correctAnswer: Rice, lentils (dahl), spices (cumin, coriander, turmeric), ghee, and flatbreads (naan, chapatti).

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on British & International Cuisine

questions.question: Q: Give an example of how historical trade influenced British food.
questions.correctAnswer: The Tudor spice trade introduced cinnamon, pepper, and nutmeg to Britain. Sugar from Caribbean plantations became affordable in the 18th century. Tea from China and India became the national drink.

questions.question: Q: What is fusion cuisine? Give an example.
questions.correctAnswer: Fusion cuisine combines elements from different culinary traditions. Examples: chicken tikka masala (Indian spices with British cream-based sauce), sushi burrito (Japanese-Mexican), ramen burger (Japanese-American).

questions.question: Q: Name a regional British dish and its region.
questions.correctAnswer: Cornish pasty (Cornwall), haggis (Scotland), Welsh rarebit (Wales), Lancashire hotpot (Lancashire), Bakewell tart (Derbyshire) (any one).

questions.question: Q: What cooking technique is associated with Chinese cuisine?
questions.correctAnswer: Stir-frying: fast cooking at high heat in a wok, which preserves nutrients, colour, and texture while using little oil.

questions.question: Q: Why is it important to study international cuisine in Food Preparation & Nutrition?
questions.correctAnswer: It broadens understanding of ingredients, cooking techniques, and cultural food practices; supports adapting recipes for different dietary needs; and reflects the multicultural reality of modern British food choice.
